prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1406; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the northbound frontage road in Conroe, Texas, waiting for traffic to clear, when Driver 2 approached from behind and struck the rear of the vehicle. Driver 2 stated that he was looking down at a phone and did not notice the stopped traffic until it was too late to brake. The impact pushed Driver 1's vehicle forward into the lane ahead, and the rear bumper and trunk lid show crush damage that is consistent with the force described at the scene. Driver 1 reported neck and back pain immediately after the collision and was assisted from the vehicle by responding units. A Passenger seated in the front right seat was also present and was confirmed by responding officers as being in the vehicle at the time of impact. Witnesses in a nearby vehicle gave statements that matched the sequence reported by both drivers, and scene photographs support their accounts. Some old scratches were noted on the lower rear bumper, which may predate this collision and were recorded for reference only. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy in force at the time of the crash.
